fluff.overview:
The Bandersnatch is a 75-ton heavy BattleMech first produced in 3052 by Bander BattleMechs, a small manufacturer on Terra Firma founded by Felifious Bander, a former chief technician of the Twelfth Star Guard. Conceived as an affordable and effective platform for mercenary commands left equipment-poor in the wake of the Clan Invasion, the Bandersnatch was the first original design offered by Bander's company after years of performing upgrades and refits on older BattleMechs using recovered technology.

Deliberately modeled on the popular Marauder to ensure a large supply of compatible replacement parts, the Bandersnatch offers a versatile heavy weapons platform at a fraction of the cost of frontline assault designs. The design has earned a solid reputation among mercenary commands and independent worlds for its reliability, affordability, and ease of maintenance.
fluff.capabilities:
The Bandersnatch's weapons array is built around the armament configurations most frequently requested by Bander's mercenary clientele. A pair of Armstrong Class-B ClusterGuns LB 10-X autocannons serve as the primary striking weapons, capable of firing both solid slugs for concentrated damage and cluster munitions effective against lighter targets and conventional aircraft. Three Holly LRM-5 racks provide sustained long-range fire support, while six Magna Mk II medium lasers (four forward-firing and two rear-mounted) ensure comprehensive close-range coverage. CASE-protected ammunition bins in both torsos mitigate the risk posed by the considerable stores of autocannon and missile reloads.

Powered by a Vlar 300 XL engine, the Bandersnatch achieves a respectable cruising speed of 43 kilometers per hour, adequate for its intended fire support role though insufficient for rapid repositioning. Eleven tons of Valiant Chainmail armor provide solid protection without maximizing the chassis's potential capacity, a deliberate cost-saving measure that even so leaves the design well-protected for its weight class. Double heat sinks allow the heavy weapons loadout to fire without significant thermal buildup, though sustained alpha strikes still demand careful heat management. Early production models exhibited a design flaw where the rear-firing lasers melted their heat jackets, requiring the weapons to be raised and ongoing field monitoring of the affected components.
fluff.history:
The Bandersnatch emerged from the chaos and desperation that followed the Clan Invasion of 3049. Felifious Bander, a veteran chief technician of the Twelfth Star Guard, leveraged his reputation and connections to recruit fellow mercenary technicians left without employment after the Clans destroyed their parent units. His company, Bander BattleMechs, began by performing upgrades on aging BattleMechs using technology recovered in the wake of the invasion, building expertise and capital before attempting an original design. The Bandersnatch, which first rolled off the assembly floor in 3052, was the culmination of that effort, a heavy 'Mech deliberately designed to be built with limited industrial resources.

Early production was extremely limited, with each machine requiring months of painstaking hand assembly. Barely a half-dozen existed by 3055, making the Bandersnatch more curiosity than contender on the mercenary market. The partnership with Kressly WarWorks on Epsilon Eridani proved transformative, as Kressly's interest in a heavy design simple enough for small-scale production opened the door to expanded manufacturing. This collaboration gave the Bandersnatch access to broader distribution networks and the industrial base of the Chaos March.

The Bandersnatch found its strongest customer base among mercenary commands and the independent worlds of the Chaos March, where its affordability and reliance on widely available Marauder-compatible components made it particularly attractive. The design's growing presence in the region drew attention from the Capellan Confederation and Trinity Alliance, who viewed the armed independence of Chaos March worlds with increasing concern.

The Jihad brought both opportunity and crisis to Bander BattleMechs. During the early years of the conflict, the company supported the Word of Blake's rule over Terra Firma, viewing the Blakists as a source of stability and profiting from 'Mech sales to their forces. This relationship soured as the full extent of Blakist atrocities became known, and the founder's own son defied his father to join the anti-Blakist resistance. The 01Ar refit variant, developed specifically to counter Blakist C3i networks, became one of the design's most widely adopted configurations during this period. Following the Jihad, the Bandersnatch continued to serve as a mainstay of mercenary and periphery forces, its reputation for reliability and affordability ensuring steady demand even as larger manufacturers competed for market share in the post-war rebuilding era.
fluff.deployment: Introduced around 3065, the 01B represents Bander's most significant revision of the original design. The defining change is the replacement of the Vlar 300 XL engine with a light fusion engine, dramatically improving survivability by allowing the 'Mech to sustain side torso damage without catastrophic engine failure, while also reducing the variant's cost by more than three million C-bills. The weapons array has been comprehensively redesigned, mounting a Magna Hellstar PPC and an Imperator Automatic Ultra AC/10 as the primary armament, supplemented by a pair of Holly LRM-5 launchers and a Holly Streak SRM-2. Four medium lasers provide close defense, and the troublesome rear-firing lasers of the original model have been eliminated entirely in favor of additional armor protection. CASE in the left torso provides ammunition protection for the revised loadout.
